name: Poach
summary: Poaching is stepping across to take a ball that was heading for your partner. Done at the right moment it turns a neutral dink into a putaway; done at the wrong one it leaves half the court open. The judgement, not the volley, is the skill.
whenToUse: The ball is floating through the middle at or above net height.
Your partner is being pulled wide and is reaching, not set.
You are the one with the forehand in the middle.
You can get there and still be balanced — a poach you have to lunge for is not one.
howTo: Watch the ball off their paddle, not your partner.
Move across on a diagonal rather than sideways, so you finish moving forward.
Take it in front of your body with a short punch, not a swing.
Hit down at the nearest opponent's feet or into the space between them.
Call it — one word, early and loud, so your partner covers behind you.
Keep going through to the side you have crossed into and let your partner take yours.
commonMistakes: Poaching a ball below the net, where you have travelled several feet to hit a dink.
Going silently, so both of you arrive at the same ball or neither does.
Reaching across without moving the feet, which leaks the volley into the net.
Poaching and then trying to get back, which leaves you nowhere at all.
Doing it constantly, at which point they aim down the line you keep abandoning.

drills.name: Middle balls only
drills.description: Two of you at the kitchen line against a feeder who sends balls deliberately through the middle at varying heights. Only the high ones may be poached, and you must call every one.

drills.name: Cross and stay
drills.description: Same drill, but after every poach the pair has to finish the rally with the sides swapped. It builds the habit of covering rather than scrambling back.

drills.name: Step across the empty side
drills.description: A feeder at the kitchen line sends dinks and floats toward the side a partner would be covering. You start on your own side and take only the balls above net height, stepping across on a diagonal and finishing on the far side. With nobody there to collide with, the drill is about reading the height and committing early.
